Lesser
les'-sēr
adj. (smaller; the inferior of two, chiefly of the moon, of cattle, and of the temple settles)
A double comparative — less already being comparative — retained in English because the Authorized Version fixed it there. Webster notes the irregularity and keeps the word for its established usage.

Biblical Definition

“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night” (Gen 1:16). Moses will not name the sun and moon. The peoples around Israel worshipped them under their names, and the fourth day of creation deliberately reduces them to two lamps and a note that God made the stars also. The lesser light is a governor, and it governs by borrowed light — it has no fire of its own, and its rule over the night is the reflection of a light it does not generate. The church has read the moon this way ever since, and rightly: every derived authority in Scripture — magistrate, elder, husband, father — is a lesser light with a real office and no independent glory. The word appears twice more, in the plain speech of the land and the sanctuary. Isaiah's desolated hill country becomes pasture “for the treading of lesser cattle” (Isa 7:25), sheep and goats grazing where vineyards were. And Ezekiel measures the altar of his temple vision from “the lesser settle even to the greater settle” (Eze 43:14) — the altar rising in ordered ledges, each one measured, the lesser real and necessary and not the greater.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines lesser as a barbarous corruption of less, formed by the vulgar from the habit of terminating comparatives in er, but established by usage — less in quantity, degree or dignity.

expand to see more

LESSER, a. This word is a corruption; but is authorized by custom, and may be sometimes useful to poetry.

1. Less; smaller; as the lesser light to rule the night. Genesis 1.

LESS, a. Smaller; not so large or great; as a less quantity; a less degree.

1. Inferior in dignity, condition or excellence.

Key Scripture

Gen 1:16 — "And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also."

Isa 7:25 — "And on all hills that shall be digged with the mattock, there shall not come thither the fear of briers and thorns: but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of lesser cattle."

Eze 43:14 — "And from the bottom upon the ground even to the lower settle shall be two cubits, and the breadth one cubit; and from the lesser settle even to the greater settle shall be four cubits, and the breadth one cubit."

Modern Corruption

“The lesser of two evils” is treated as a biblical category; Genesis 1 uses the word for a real office under a greater light.

expand to see more

The phrase most people meet the word in — the lesser of two evils — is not a biblical idiom and imports a moral calculus Scripture does not use. The Bible has a category for choosing rightly under constraint, and it is the doctrine of lawful callings and providence, not a scale on which sins are weighed against each other and the lighter one chosen. Where Scripture uses lesser, it is describing something genuinely good that is genuinely subordinate: a light, a herd, a ledge of the altar. The lesser light is not a lesser evil. It is a servant with a station.

The principle to recover is subordination without contempt. Moses could have named the moon and did not; he ranked it. Every derived office in the household of God is a lesser light — deacon under elder, child under parent, wife under husband in the creational order, magistrate under Christ — and the modern instinct is to hear any such ranking as an insult. Genesis 1 hears it as an appointment. The lesser light rules; it simply does not shine on its own.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew qaton (H6996), small, lesser, younger; ma'or (H3974), luminary, light-bearer; tso'n (H6629), the flock, small cattle.

expand to see more

Hebrew qaton (H6996) — small, little, younger; Genesis 1:16, the lesser (smaller) light.

Hebrew ma'or (H3974) — a luminary, a light-holder; the word Moses uses instead of naming the sun and moon.

Hebrew tso'n (H6629) — flock, small cattle, sheep and goats; Isaiah 7:25.

Hebrew 'azarah (H5835) — a ledge or settle of the altar; Ezekiel 43:14, the lesser and the greater settle.

Greek elasson (G1640) — less, smaller, younger; Romans 9:12, the elder shall serve the younger; Hebrews 7:7, the less is blessed of the better.

Usage

"“The lesser light to rule the night” — a real rule, on borrowed light."

"“The treading of lesser cattle” — vineyards turned to pasture in judgment."

"“From the lesser settle even to the greater” — the altar rose in measured ranks."
